Reviewer A found two warning-level correctness defects. No fixes were made.

1. **warning** — `/tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py:21`: Adjacent intervals incorrectly conflict. `_conflicts` uses inclusive comparisons at both ends. After `b.reserve('room', 10, 20)`, both `b.available('room', 0, 10)` and `b.available('room', 20, 30)` return `False`; reserving either interval raises `ValueError`. Half-open intervals share no occupied time in these cases, so availability should be `True` and reservation should succeed. Both public methods call this predicate after validation, making the defect reachable using the declared string/integer types. Static inspection and Python runtime probes confirmed both boundary directions. Minimal remedy: use `start < existing_end and existing_start < end`.

2. **warning** — `/tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py:43`: Cancelling an unknown or previously cancelled ID raises `KeyError` instead of returning `False`. `dict.pop(id)` has no default, so execution raises before evaluating `is not None` when the ID is absent. A runtime probe reserved ID `'0'`, cancelled it successfully with `True`, then observed `KeyError('0')` on the second cancellation. `cancel('not-issued')` also raised `KeyError`. These are ordinary public API calls with string IDs. Minimal remedy: use `self._live.pop(id, None) is not None`; live values are always tuples.

Scope: `/tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py`, assessed against the supplied ReservationBook intent. Two warning findings; no fixes made.

Full report: [report.md](/tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/reports/reviewer-B/report.md).

## Findings

1. **warning — Adjacent half-open intervals are treated as overlapping.**

   Exact location: [reservations.py:21](/tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py:21).

   `_conflicts` uses `start <= existing_end and existing_start <= end`. Equality at either endpoint therefore counts as overlap, although half-open intervals sharing only an endpoint do not overlap. Both public callers are affected: `reserve` calls this predicate at line 28 and raises ValueError; `available` negates it at line 39 and reports False.

   Runtime evidence: after `b.reserve('room', 10, 20)`, both `b.available('room', 0, 10)` and `b.available('room', 20, 30)` returned False; reserving either adjacent interval raised `ValueError('reservation overlaps an existing booking')`. These are valid string/int calls within the stated contract. Users cannot book back-to-back reservations on the same resource.

   Minimal remedy: use strict inequalities for both endpoint comparisons.

2. **warning — Unknown and repeated cancellation raise instead of returning False.**

   Exact location: [reservations.py:43](/tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py:43).

   `self._live.pop(id)` has no default, so a missing ID raises KeyError before the `is not None` comparison runs. This affects an unknown ID immediately and any valid ID after its first successful cancellation.

   Runtime evidence: the first `b.cancel(rid)` returned True and freed the interval; the second raised `KeyError('0')`. `b.cancel('never-issued')` also raised KeyError. Callers expecting the documented boolean result instead encounter an exception on these required state transitions.

   Minimal remedy: supply a None default to `pop`; stored live values are tuples, so None distinguishes absence.

## Actual commands and checks

- `pwd; rg --files -g '*' /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project` — project inventory contained only `reservations.py` and `user-notes.txt`.
- `sha256sum /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/user-notes.txt; nl -ba /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py; cat /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/user-notes.txt` — inspected the complete source and read-only notes; both pinned hashes matched.
- `python -B - <<'PY' ... PY` — initial behavioral-probe attempt failed with exit 127: `python: command not found`. No Python code executed in this attempt.
- `python3 -B - <<'PY' ... PY` — executed an in-memory probe using `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, `module_from_spec`, and `exec_module` to load the exact source path. Exit 0. Results:
  - Reproduced both adjacency failures on each side of an existing `[10,20)` reservation.
  - Five true overlap cases, `[10,20)`, `[11,19)`, `[9,21)`, `[9,11)`, and `[19,21)`, correctly returned unavailable and raised ValueError on reserve, preserving live bookings and the ID counter.
  - Same-time reservations on a different resource and a separated `[21,30)` interval succeeded.
  - Both reserve and available rejected `('',0,1)`, `('room',1,1)`, and `('room',2,1)` with ValueError, preserving live bookings and the ID counter in all six calls.
  - Available calls for occupied and unused resources preserved live bookings and the ID counter.
  - First cancellation returned True; repeated and unknown cancellations reproduced the KeyError finding; the cancelled interval became available.
  - Four reserve/cancel cycles alternating between two additional books produced IDs distinct from all previously issued IDs in the probe.
- `sha256sum /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/reservations.py /tmp/jstack-interrogate-tzccn3tn/project/user-notes.txt` — repeated after inspection and probes; unchanged.

The Python probe mutated only imported in-memory objects. `-B` disabled bytecode writes. After reserving `('r',10,20)`, availability for `(0,10)` and `(20,30)` returns False, and reserving `(20,30)` raises ValueError. This blocks valid back-to-back bookings and misreports availability. The smallest remedy is a None default for pop, since stored values are tuples.
